correctness.rationale: For |z|<2, S(z)=1+sum_{n≥1}z^n/(2^n−1)=1+sum_{j≥1}z/(2^j−z), by absolute double-series convergence. Thus S(−x)=1−F(x), F(x)=sum_j x/(2^j+x), strictly increasing and continuous for 0<x<2. F(1)<sum_j2^(−j)=1. An independent fractions.Fraction evaluation of the six terms at x=3/2 returns 65011734/64203755=1+807979/64203755, strictly exceeding 1. Therefore the unique α∈(1,3/2) with S(−α)=0 is simple since S′(−α)=sum_j 2^j/(2^j+α)^2>0. The pole of the analytic reciprocal 1/S at −α forces Taylor radius R≤α<3/2, contradicting b_n=O(2^(−n)), which would imply R≥2 by Cauchy–Hadamard. Independent root computation places α≈1.4285065080 but is not a proof of uniqueness; monotonicity is. No claim about nonreal zeros, leading coefficient asymptotics or improving the arithmetic alternating-sum remainder.
